caption: The drawing consists entirely of handwritten text in pencil on a light beige sheet of paper. The text is organized in a single block and describes in detail the construction and assembly of a coat and vest, with sections labeled for each garment. The descriptions reference numerous lettered parts (e.g., "A-A1," "B-B1") and contain specific sewing and assembly instructions using terminology such as seams, flaps, darts, collars, pockets, and facings. Punctuation marks and symbols such as underlines, arrows, "T," "V," and "W" are used to denote specific marks or actions in the assembly process. The handwriting is consistent and neat, generally using uppercase letters with a few underlined or parenthesized words for emphasis. The composition is framed with a single-line border drawn around the text block. There are no illustrations, patterns, or images—only text and instructional notes. The top left bears the handwritten note “Plate 4,” while across the upper edge are the words “L. 928 A-B-C COAT.”
title: Written Instructions for Making Suit
